prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats pitch themselves as the real, constructive opposition to a hard-Brexit Conservative government and a weak Labour Party. Their vision is an open, tolerant, united Britain that protects rights, invests in people and places, and works closely with Europe. They rule out coalition with either Conservatives or Corbyn’s Labour.

Europe and Brexit: They accept the 2016 mandate to negotiate but reject a hard Brexit. They demand a referendum on the final deal with the option to remain. Priorities include: guaranteeing EU/UK citizens’ rights; keeping the UK in the single market and customs union; protecting freedom of movement; safeguarding Erasmus+; upholding social and environmental standards; maintaining Europol, the EAW and data-sharing; defending science funding; and respecting the interests of Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and Gibraltar.

NHS and Social Care: To tackle a systemic funding crisis, they propose a 1p rise on all income tax bands ringfenced for the NHS and social care, with a long-term dedicated health and care tax. They will integrate health and care, cap social care costs, end the NHS pay freeze, restore nurse bursaries, and deliver true parity for mental health with waiting-time standards, more talking therapies, and crisis care that ends police-cell use.

Education and Opportunity: They will invest nearly £7bn more in schools and the Pupil Premium, oppose new grammars, restore local oversight of places, and raise teacher pay and development. Early years get a tripled Early Years Pupil Premium and more qualified staff. Universities: reinstate maintenance grants, protect research and EU collaboration, and review funding fairly. Lifelong learning: expand apprenticeships, address skills gaps, and support adult retraining.

Economy and Fair Taxes: Eliminate the day-to-day deficit by 2020 but borrow £100bn for infrastructure (homes, hospitals, schools, broadband, rail). Protect NHS/social care via the 1p rise and schools per-pupil funding; end the 1% public-sector pay cap. Crack down on avoidance, reform business rates, and consider land value taxation. Support SMEs via an expanded British Business Bank and a start-up allowance. Modernise work: promote a genuine living wage, curb zero-hours abuses, strengthen rights in the gig economy, and boost employee ownership.

Green Leadership: Pass five green laws; retrofit four million homes; ban new diesel car/small van sales by 2025; expand clean transport zones; reach 60% renewable electricity by 2030; oppose fracking; pursue zero carbon by 2050; protect nature, farming standards and fisheries; drive a circular economy with a Zero-Waste Act.

Homes, Families, Communities: Build 300,000 homes a year (including 500,000 affordable), create new garden cities, lift council borrowing caps, and reform renting (ban fees, cap deposits, longer tenancies). Expand free childcare from nine months for working parents over time; add a month of “use it or lose it” paternity leave. Improve buses and rail; introduce a young person’s bus discount.

Rights, Justice, Immigration: Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; enact a digital bill of rights; tackle hate crime; expand refugee resettlement (50,000 Syrians; reopen Dubs, end indefinite detention). Reform justice to reduce reoffending; decriminalise drug possession for personal use and create a regulated cannabis market.

Global Role and Security: Stay internationalist, support the UN/NATO, maintain 0.7% aid, restrict arms to rights abusers (suspend sales to Saudi Arabia), invest in cyber, keep a minimum nuclear deterrent with three boats, and lead on disarmament.

Fix the System: Introduce STV for Westminster and local elections, votes at 16, a reformed elected Lords, tighter party funding rules, and a federal UK with deeper devolution—including “devolution on demand” in England—while opposing Scottish independence.
